evals.name: orders-from-skeleton
evals.prompt: This service is just a skeleton so far. Add orders over HTTP: place an order (customer ID + total in cents), get an order, and cancel an order. An order can't be cancelled twice. The shipping team (not in this repo yet) will need to react when orders are placed or cancelled. Keep storage in memory for now.
evals.expected_output: Place/cancel commands, a get query with a read model, OrderPlaced/OrderCancelled events, correct error mapping, registration in main.go, tests; no worked example exists in the fixture to copy from.

assertions.text: The Order aggregate (internal/ordering/domain) keeps private state, validates on creation, and has a Cancel method that rejects a second cancel with a domain error
OrderPlaced and OrderCancelled events embed events.Base, carry the order's aggregate ID, and have exported past-tense name constants prefixed with the context (e.g. ordering.order_placed)

PlaceOrder and CancelOrder are commands whose handlers return only ([]events.Event, error) — the order ID is generated by the caller, not returned by the command — and return PullEvents() after saving
GetOrder is a query whose handler returns a read model/DTO, not the aggregate
Command and query Name() methods return constants (value receiver, no fields used), so RegisterCommand/RegisterQuery route correctly
A domain ErrNotFound is returned by the repository; HTTP maps not found → 404, already cancelled → 409, invalid input → 400/422
Use cases are registered (in main.go or a helper it calls) via cqrs.RegisterCommand/RegisterQuery with the shared middleware, and registration errors are checked
No empty or no-op event handlers are registered just to make publishing succeed
The response tells the user that event consumers must be idempotent and/or that in-process events can be lost on crash (outbox for durability)
Tests cover the cancel rule and the handlers
go vet ./... and go test ./... pass

Events are published only after the state change is committed (via WithUnitOfWork or an equivalent), and a command that succeeded but whose events failed to publish (ErrEventsNotPublished) is not reported to the client as an error
Expected domain rejections (not found, already cancelled, invalid input) are not logged at ERROR level
The in-memory repository stores state (a record/snapshot/copy without pending events), not the live aggregate pointer, so loading an order never replays old events

evals.name: new-invoicing-service
evals.prompt: Start a new Go service in this empty directory for managing invoices (module github.com/acme/invoicing). It needs to: create an invoice, mark an invoice as paid, and list unpaid invoices, all over HTTP. Later we'll want to send emails when an invoice is paid, so design for that. In-memory storage is fine for now.
evals.expected_output: A new module with the platform installed under internal/platform, a bounded context with domain/app/infra layers, two commands and one query, an InvoicePaid event, composition root in cmd/, tests; everything compiles.

assertions.text: go.mod declares module github.com/acme/invoicing
Platform packages (bus, cqrs, events, ddd) exist under internal/platform with imports rewritten to github.com/acme/invoicing
Layout: thin main under cmd/<name>/, and an invoicing bounded context split into domain, app and infra packages; domain imports neither app nor infra
Create and mark-paid are commands (handlers return events and error); list-unpaid is a query returning a read model/DTO, not aggregates
Marking an invoice as paid is a domain method that enforces a rule (e.g. can't pay twice) and records an InvoicePaid event
Events are published after the state change is committed, so a future email handler only needs to subscribe (no changes to the pay use case)
HTTP adapters only decode, dispatch to the application layer and encode; domain errors map to 4xx codes (not found → 404, conflict → 409, invalid input → 400 or 422)
The in-memory repository stores state (a record/snapshot/copy without pending events), not the live aggregate pointer
The design is proportionate: no outbox, retry relay or mailer implementation built before the user asked for emails (mentioning them as next steps is fine)
Tests exist for the domain and/or handlers
go vet ./... and go test ./... pass
Expected domain rejections (not found, already paid, invalid input) are not logged at ERROR level

evals.name: review-billing-subtle
evals.prompt: Review the internal/billing code in this repo. A teammate wrote it, it compiles and looks fine to me, but I want a second pair of eyes before we ship. List the problems you find with file:line and how you'd fix them. Don't change any code.
evals.expected_output: A review that finds the 8 planted, subtler violations (several only visible at runtime) with locations and concrete fixes, and modifies no files.

assertions.text: Finds that PayInvoice.Name() depends on a field (app/pay_invoice.go:13), so RegisterCommand registers it under the zero-value name and every dispatch fails as not dispatchable
Finds that GET /invoices/{id} asks for *app.InvoiceView while the handler returns app.InvoiceView (infra/httpapi/handlers.go:55), so every request fails with ErrUnexpectedResult
Finds that charging the customer is not idempotent (app/charge_customer.go): a redelivered event charges twice; suggests a dedupe key such as the invoice ID
Finds that events.Register is called twice for the same event name with the error ignored (cmd/shop/main.go:~88), so NotifyAccountingWhenInvoiceIssued is never registered
Finds that IssueInvoiceHandler ignores the Save error and still returns events (app/issue_invoice.go:26)
Finds that the issued event is named imperatively / like the command (IssueInvoiceEvent, "billing.issue_invoice" at domain/invoice.go:13) instead of past tense
Finds that the issued event uses uuid.Nil() as aggregate ID (domain/invoice.go:47) instead of the invoice ID
Finds that PayInvoiceHandler changes state and records the event itself (app/pay_invoice.go:22-29, exported Status) instead of a domain method like inv.Pay()
Each of the eight planted problems above that the review finds comes with a file:line and a concrete fix
No files in the project were modified

Finds that the in-memory store persists the aggregate including its pending events (infra/memory/store.go:~22), so loading an invoice to pay it republishes IssueInvoiceEvent and charges the customer again
